Synthetic action binding oracle, authored for Task 5 (14 October 2026).

The adjacent action-binding.jcs is frozen literal expected canonical bytes, with
no trailing newline. Every character is ASCII; the only scalar domains are
strings, exact safe integers and one boolean. This restricted fixture makes
stdlib json.dumps(binding, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8") identical to RFC 8785 without importing or
calling the SDK or its RFC 8785 dependency. hashlib.sha256 independently computes:

e3860ea56b81199fb42870a5ee4e17bc0d4c90e54026fe2d36e21debd5cc7c7c

The test compares the entire committed literal byte artifact and literal hash,
then revalidates both dictionary and typed intent forms. The fresh fixture uses
only synthetic IDs and repeated-character hashes. No customer data or external
record/provenance claims are present. This oracle does not replace the broader
independent ECMAScript JCS coverage in the foundational canonical tests.
